sentences.text: Allognathosuchus is an extinct genus of alligatorine crocodylians, a name meaning 'other jaw crocodile'.
This medium-sized predator could reach lengths of up to 1.5 meters.
Its skull featured robust jaws and large, rounded teeth situated toward the back of both the upper and lower tooth rows.
Scientists historically viewed these specialized teeth as tools adapted for crushing mollusks.
In 2004, researcher Christopher Brochu advised using the genus name conservatively because the available remains were often incomplete.
The animal lived from the Campanian to the Priabonian stages, spanning between 83.6 and 33.9 million years ago.
Although recent studies consistently place A. polyodon and A. wartheni within Alligatorinae, their exact relative placement within the group remains disputed.
